A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIM research, retaining the synthetic-training framework, local ODE estimator and several benchmarks. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial changes in title, scope and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original FIM experiments on ODEBench and Lorenz trajectories, alongside motion-capture and Navier-Stokes imputation demonstrations and ETT interpolation.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction, derivative-estimation and imputation results, including extensive benchmark comparisons and architecture, training-data and windowing ablations.

M1.justification: v2 adds a learned temporal-gap imputation module above the frozen local estimator FIM-ℓ: a transformer processes local embeddings and scale statistics to predict the missing interval's representation, followed by boundary-conditioned integration (Section 3.2.2; Appendix C). This substantially extends v1's upsampling and window-composition approach. The stated local reconstruction objective also changes from squared to absolute error.

E1.justification: v2 adds air-quality, traffic, solar-power, electricity and healthcare evaluations, including PhysioNet2012 and PhysioNet2019 in Appendix F. It also adds single-coordinate phase-portrait reconstruction and four synthetic regression tasks. ODEBench, Lorenz, motion capture and Navier-Stokes remain; the separate ETTh2, ETTm1 and ETTm2 interpolation demonstrations from v1 disappear.

E2.justification: Reported comparisons expand substantially to include Neural ODE Processes, BRITS, SAITS, GP-VAE, CSDI, BayOTIDE and numerous additional imputation methods. Cubic splines join the retained Lorenz comparison, while motion-capture comparisons include LatentODE, npODE, GPDM and VGPLVM. ODEFormer, ODEFormer-opt and PySR remain in v2 Table 9; their move out of the main comparison is not removal.

E3.justification: The default local-model training dataset changes from 8M to 2M trajectories, with revised sampling distributions and a separate temporal-gap training dataset. Evaluation adds window sweeps and derivative scoring. Lorenz corruption is described as additive rather than v1's multiplicative noise. Motion capture and Navier-Stokes expand from single examples to 43 and 61 trajectories, with PCA and direct-space evaluation. v2 inconsistently states minimum contexts of four and eight observations.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled studies of parameter count, training-set size, BiLSTM versus transformer encoding, context limits, temporal-gap sizes and training trends (Tables 4-8). It also studies window-count sensitivity, including the Lorenz sweep in Figure 8, and PCA versus direct-space imputation. v1's explicit FIM denoising comparison with and without Savitzky-Golay filtering is not retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ODEBench variation across ten corruption realizations and trajectory-level standard deviations. v2 additionally displays predictive derivative uncertainty in Figure 3 and identifies imported TSI-Bench baseline deviations as coming from five training rounds (Tables 21-22). These extend uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in repeated FIM training runs.

E6.justification: Existing scores are replaced and substantial new results appear. At 50% subsampling and noise 0.05, v1 Table 1 reports R2 accuracy of 80.2 ± 1.7 for FIM and 79.6 ± 1.5 for FIM-N; v2 Table 9 reports 83.7 ± 0.7 for four-window FIM-ℓ and 91.6 ± 1.9 for sixteen windows. These involve revised configurations, not controlled version-to-version gains. New results include derivative errors, quantitative imputation comparisons and clinical-data failures.

T1.justification: The path-wise ODE reduction and overlapping-window interpolation are retained. v2 adds derivations for rescaling derivatives and variances (Appendix B.1) and constructing continuous solutions across a missing interval (Appendix C.6), while removing v1's alternative kernel-operator formulation. These are localized mathematical developments rather than a new theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: v1 presents a general program for zero-shot ODE-system inference, with imputation as an application. v2 makes zero-shot imputation of hidden ODE solutions the central contribution, explicitly separating point-wise and temporal missingness, and adds phase-portrait reconstruction from one observed coordinate as a headline capability. Arbitrary-dimensional application without downstream fine-tuning remains a core claim.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanation of applicability and failure. It distinguishes local interpolation from global information needed across temporal gaps, explains normalization problems for nearly constant noisy signals, and identifies sparse-coordinate failures of channel independence using PhysioNet. It also discusses window-resolution tradeoffs, rapid-derivative failures and errors introduced by PCA. v1's limitations mainly concerned high-frequency dynamics and its approximately 32-point context requirement.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents normalization and output rescaling, detailed temporal-module architecture and optimization, dataset masks and preprocessing, and LatentODE search grids, training schedules and runtimes. It also reports high-dimensional inference costs and describes a reproduction script. The availability statement changes from pretrained models being online in v1 to forthcoming online availability in v2, although supplementary code and weights are still asserted.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts from ODE identification and analogies with language models toward amortized inference and time-series imputation. v2 adds discussion and citations for Stuhlmüller, Paige and Wood, zero-shot learning, channel-independent modeling, and major imputation families and benchmarks. Much of v1's neural-ODE training and transfer-learning discussion is removed. ODEFormer's preprint-to-publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten around imputation. Experiments are reorganized into phase-portrait reconstruction and two missingness categories; limitations are integrated into the conclusion, and a reproducibility statement is added. The appendices are substantially reorganized into model-specific documentation and task-specific evaluations, beyond simply appending new experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v2 introduces a graphical-model/architecture schematic, phase portraits, derivative-uncertainty panels and a window-sensitivity plot. Lorenz plots are redesigned to include derivatives, and tables become extensive window/dimension breakdowns and benchmark matrices, including landscape appendix tables. v1's ETT panels and Navier-Stokes image demonstration are removed.

improvement.justification: v1's imputation evidence was largely illustrative. v2 supplies an explicit temporal-gap method, broad quantitative comparisons, controlled ablations, detailed implementation information and concrete failure analyses, substantially strengthening validation and reproducibility. Reporting problems remain: minimum-context specifications conflict, Table 23's Navier-Stokes RMSE contradicts the claimed benefit of avoiding PCA, and Table 22 shows linear interpolation outperforming FIM on some datasets highlighted favorably in Table 2. These qualifications limit particular claims but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidential support.
